		% % ---
		\paragraph{Genesis 1:2} % *GENESIS-1-2
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-1-2}

			And the earth was
				\footnote{%
					``Without form, and void'' translates \he{tohU wAbohU}. On 5 January 1841, in \hyperlink{EMS-1841-JS-5-JAN-1841-WC-e}{notes taken by William Clayton}, JS is recorded as saying that these Hebrew words should be translated as ``empty and desolate.'' PPP also gives this translation in his 1840 ``Regeneration,'' where he renders the verse as, ``and the earth she was empty and desolate; and darkness upon the faces of the abyss; and the wind of God was brooding over the faces of the waters'' (109). Note that the version of the verse in Moses has the original KJV language, while the version in Abraham has ``empty and desolate.'' The Moses version is from around December 1830, while the Abraham dates to March 1842. It seems likely that JS adopted the ``empty and desolate'' language after he started learning Hebrew. In Seixas's 1834 \textit{Hebrew Grammar}, the nouns \he{t*ohU} and \he{b*ohU} are glossed as ``empty'' and ``desolate,'' respectively (78).
					}%
			without form, and void;%
				\footnote{%
					% \label{}%
					For a good extended (and very technical) discussion of the meaning of \he{tohU wAbohU}, see EWING 17--43. Tsumura's conclusion involves saying that the phrase has nothing to do with chaos or disorganization. Quoting from page 43: ``In conclusion, both the biblical context and extra-biblical parallels suggest that the phrase \textit{tōhû wābōhû} in Gen 1:2 has nothing to do with `chaos' and simply means `emptiness' and refers to the earth which is an empty place, i.e. `an unproductive and uninhabited place.' Thus, the main reason for the author's mentioning the earth as \textit{tōhû wābōhû} in this setting is to inform the audience that the earth is `not yet' the earth as it was known to them. As Westermann notes, `creation and the world are to be understood always from the viewpoint of or in the context of human existence.' In other words, to communicate the subject of creation to human beings it is impossible to avoid using the language and literary forms known to them. In order to give the background information, the author uses experiential language in this verse, to explain the initial situation of the earth as `not yet.''' This conclusion goes well with JS's take, though he got that from Seixas.
					}
			and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{וְהָאָ֗רֶץ הָיְתָ֥ה תֹ֙הוּ֙ וָבֹ֔הוּ וְחֹ֖שֶׁךְ עַל־פְּנֵ֣י תְה֑וֹם וְר֣וּחַ אֱלֹהִ֔ים מְרַחֶ֖פֶת עַל־פְּנֵ֥י הַמָּֽיִם׃}
					\item[LXX] \gr{ἡ δὲ γῆ ἦν ἀόρατος καὶ ἀκατασκεύαστος, καὶ σκότος ἐπάνω τῆς ἀβύσσου, καὶ πνεῦµα θεοῦ ἐπεφέρετο ἐπάνω τοῦ ὕδατος.}
					\item[BSV] terra autem erat inanis et vacua et tenebrae super faciem abyssi et spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas
					% \item[AB ]
					\item[NETS] Yet the earth was invisible and unformed, and darkness was over the abyss, and a divine wind was being carried along over the water.

					% \item[OTR1]

					\item[NRSV] the earth was a formless void and darkness covered the face of the deep, while a wind from God swept over the face of the waters.
					\item[VULGATE] Terra autem erat inanis et vacua, et tenebræ erant super faciem abyssi: et Spiritus Dei ferebatur super aquas.

		\paragraph{Genesis 2:8} % *GENESIS-2-8
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-2-8}

			And the LORD God planted a garden eastward in Eden;%
				\footnote{%
					The Syriac Peshitta gives this passage as, ``Then the Lord God planted Paradise in Eden from the east.'' But the editors include this note: ``See the discussion on this verse in Piet Dirksen, `The Peshitta and Textual Criticism of the Old Testament,' \textit{VT} 42 (1992), 378. He translates the Peshi\d{t}ta `from of old' and notes that this reading, because it also appears in the Targum, reflects `a Jewish tradition that Paradise was created before the world'. Sokoloff-Brockelmann gloss this phrase with `in the east' (p. 1315). Both interpretations are possible.'' So if you read this as, ``God planted a garden from of old,'' as in, God had planted a garden a long time before and then put Adam in it, the garden would have to have already been there; the world he put him on would have had to exist already.
					}

			\label{GENESIS-3-8}

		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-4-1}

			And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived, and bare Cain, and said, I have gotten a man from the LORD.

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{וְהָ֣אָדָ֔ם יָדַ֖ע אֶת־חַוָּ֣ה אִשְׁתּ֑וֹ וַתַּ֙הַר֙ וַתֵּ֣לֶד אֶת־קַ֔יִן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר קָנִ֥יתִי אִ֖ישׁ אֶת־יְהוָֽה׃}

					\item[NIV] Adam made love to his wife Eve, and she became pregnant and gave birth to Cain. She said, “With the help of the LORD I have brought forth a man.”
					\item[NRSV] Now the man knew his wife Eve, and she conceived and bore Cain, saying, “I have produced a man with the help of the LORD.”
					\item[VULGATE] Adam vero cognovit uxorem suam Hevam: quæ concepit et peperit Cain, dicens: Possedi hominem per Deum.

					\item[BHS] \he{הֲל֤וֹא אִם־תֵּיטִיב֙ שְׂאֵ֔ת וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תֵיטִ֔יב לַפֶּ֖תַח חַטָּ֣את רֹבֵ֑ץ וְאֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ תְּשׁ֣וּקָת֔וֹ וְאַתָּ֖ה תִּמְשָׁל־בּֽוֹ׃}

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶל־קַ֔יִן אֵ֖י הֶ֣בֶל אָחִ֑יךָ וַיֹּ֙אמֶר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי הֲשֹׁמֵ֥ר אָחִ֖י אָנֹֽכִי׃}

	\subsubsection{Genesis 8} % *GENESIS-8
	% -----
		\label{GENESIS-8}

		% % ---
		\paragraph{Genesis 8:1} % *GENESIS-8-1
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-8-1}

			And God remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and God made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged;

			\begin{versebox}

		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-11-3}

		\paragraph{Genesis 11:5} % *GENESIS-11-5
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-11-5}

			And the LORD came down to see the city and the tower, which the children of men%
				\footnote{%
					% \label{}%
					AB 1A 396 on ``children of men'': ``The term for humans is \he{b*:ney hA'AdAM} (`sons/children of humans/Adam'), which subtly evokes their first ancestor. The transgression of the human/divine boundary by the first humans is now, in a sense, recapitulated by their descendants. What once was an individual breach of boundaries is now a collective breach, as humans attempt to ascend to heaven.'' NICOT 01a PDF 390: ``In this verse the builders are styled as \he{b*:ney hA'AdAM} (lit., `sons of Adam,' or `sons of the man'), which we have translated simply \textit{the men}. Earlier they had been referred to individually as \he{'iy+s} (lit., `man,' v. 3). The shift here to a term beginning with \he{b}- allows for alliteration with the verb \he{b*AnU}. Also, the shift reduces these pretentious human beings to their real size. They are but mere earthlings.''
					}

		\paragraph{Genesis 11:31} % *GENESIS-11-31
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-11-31}

			And Terah took Abram his son, and Lot the son of Haran his son's son, and Sarai his daughter in law, his son Abram's wife; and they went forth with them from Ur of the Chaldees, to go into the land of Canaan; and they came unto Haran, and dwelt there.

			\begin{versebox}

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{וַתֹּ֨אמֶר שָׂרַ֣י אֶל־אַבְרָם֮ חֲמָסִ֣י עָלֶיךָ֒ אָנֹכִ֗י נָתַ֤תִּי שִׁפְחָתִי֙ בְּחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וַתֵּ֙רֶא֙ כִּ֣י הָרָ֔תָה וָאֵקַ֖ל בְּעֵינֶ֑יהָ יִשְׁפֹּ֥ט יְהוָ֖ה בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽיׄךָ׃}

		\paragraph{Genesis 22:1} % *GENESIS-22-1
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-22-1}

			And it came to pass after these things, that God did tempt%
				\footnote{%
					% \label{}%
					\he{nis*Ah}, from \hyperref[NASAH]{\hel{nAsAh}}, HALOT 702a, in the piel, meaning \#1, ``to \textbf{put someone to the test},'' meaning \#2, ``to give experience, \textbf{train},'' meaning \#3, ``to \textbf{conduct a test, make an attempt}.'' HALOT lists this use in Genesis 22:1 under meaning \#1. Compare \hyperref[DEUTERONOMY-33-8]{Deuteronomy 33:8}, about Levi, and \hyperref[DANIEL-1-12]{Daniel 1:12, 14}.
					}
			Abraham, and said unto him, Abraham: and he said, Behold, here I am.

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{וַיְהִ֗י אַחַר֙ הַדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה וְהָ֣אֱלֹהִ֔ים נִסָּ֖ה אֶת־אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַבְרָהָ֖ם וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הִנֵּֽנִי׃}
					\item[LXX] \gr{Καὶ ἐγένετο µετὰ τὰ ῥήµατα ταῦτα ὁ θεὸς ἐπείραζεν τὸν Αβρααµ καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτόν Αβρααµ, Αβρααµ· ὁ δὲ εἶπεν Ἰδοὺ ἐγώ.}

					% \item[AB ]
					% \item[NETS]
					% \item[OTR1]
					% \item[OTR2]

					\item[NIV] Some time later God tested Abraham. He said to him, “Abraham!” “Here I am,” he replied.
					\item[NRSV] After these things God tested Abraham. He said to him, “Abraham!” And he said, “Here I am.”
					\item[VULGATE] Quæ postquam gesta sunt, tentavit Deus Abraham, et dixit ad eum: Abraham, Abraham. At ille respondit: Adsum.

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{שְׁמָעֵ֣נוּ ׀ אֲדֹנִ֗י נְשִׂ֨יא אֱלֹהִ֤ים אַתָּה֙ בְּתוֹכֵ֔נוּ בְּמִבְחַ֣ר קְבָרֵ֔ינוּ קְבֹ֖ר אֶת־מֵתֶ֑ךָ אִ֣ישׁ מִמֶּ֔נּוּ אֶת־קִבְר֛וֹ לֹֽא־יִכְלֶ֥ה מִמְּךָ֖ מִקְּבֹ֥ר מֵתֶֽךָ׃}

					% % \item[OTR1]

					\item[VULGATE] Audi nos domine, princeps Dei es apud nos: in electis sepulchris nostris sepeli mortuum tuum: nullusque te prohibere poterit quin in monumento eius sepelias mortuum tuum.

					% % \item[OTXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXXX*]

	% -----

		% % ---
		\paragraph{Genesis 26:1} % *GENESIS-26-1
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-26-1}

			And there was a famine in the land, beside the first famine that was in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went unto Abimelech king of the Philistines unto Gerar.

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{וַיְהִ֤י רָעָב֙ בָּאָ֔רֶץ מִלְּבַד֙ הָרָעָ֣ב הָרִאשׁ֔וֹן אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָיָ֖ה בִּימֵ֣י אַבְרָהָ֑ם וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ יִצְחָ֛ק אֶל־אֲבִימֶּ֥לֶךְ מֶֽלֶךְ־פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים גְּרָֽרָה׃}

					% % \item[AB ]
					% % \item[NETS]
					% % \item[OTR1]
					% % \item[OTR2]

					\item[NRSV] Now there was a famine in the land, besides the former famine that had occurred in the days of Abraham. And Isaac went to Gerar, to King Abimelech of the Philistines.
					\item[VULGATE] Orta autem fame super terram post eam sterilitatem, quæ acciderat in diebus Abraham, abiit Isaac ad Abimelech regem Palæstinorum in Gerara.

		\paragraph{Genesis 26:2} % *GENESIS-26-2
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-26-2}

			So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come, when it shall come for my hire before thy face: every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and brown among the sheep, that shall be counted stolen with me.

					\item[NRSV] So my honesty will answer for me later, when you come to look into my wages with you. Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats and black among the lambs, if found with me, shall be counted stolen.”

		% % ---
		\paragraph{Genesis 37:1} % *GENESIS-37-1
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-37-1}

			And Jacob dwelt in the land wherein his father was a stranger, in the land of Canaan.

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{וַיֵּ֣שֶׁב יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מְגוּרֵ֣י אָבִ֑יו בְּאֶ֖רֶץ כְּנָֽעַן׃}

					% % \item[NETS]
					% % \item[OTR1]
					% % \item[OTR2]

					\item[NIV] Jacob lived in the land where his father had stayed, the land of Canaan.
					\item[NRSV] Jacob settled in the land where his father had lived as an alien, the land of Canaan.
					\item[VULGATE] Habitavit autem Iacob in terra Chanaan, in qua pater suus peregrinatus est.
					% % \item[OTX*]
					% % \item[OTXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXXXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXXXXX*]
			\end{versebox}

		% % ---
		\paragraph{Genesis 37:2} % *GENESIS-37-2
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-37-2}

			These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren; and the lad was with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives: and Joseph brought unto his father their evil report.

			\begin{versebox}
					\item[BHS] \he{אֵ֣לֶּה ׀ תֹּלְד֣וֹת יַעֲקֹ֗ב יוֹסֵ֞ף בֶּן־שְׁבַֽע־עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ הָיָ֨ה רֹעֶ֤ה אֶת־אֶחָיו֙ בַּצֹּ֔אן וְה֣וּא נַ֗עַר אֶת־בְּנֵ֥י בִלְהָ֛ה וְאֶת־בְּנֵ֥י זִלְפָּ֖ה נְשֵׁ֣י אָבִ֑יו וַיָּבֵ֥א יוֹסֵ֛ף אֶת־דִּבָּתָ֥ם רָעָ֖ה אֶל־אֲבִיהֶֽם׃}
					% \item[LXX] \gr{}
					% \item[BSV]
					% % \item[AB ]
					% % \item[NETS]
					% % \item[OTR1]
					% % \item[OTR2]
					\item[ASV] These are the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brethren; and he was a lad with the sons of Bilhah, and with the sons of Zilpah, his father's wives: and Joseph brought the evil report of them unto their father.
					\item[NIV] This is the account of Jacob’s family line. Joseph, a young man of seventeen, was tending the flocks with his brothers, the sons of Bilhah and the sons of Zilpah, his father’s wives, and he brought their father a bad report about them.
					\item[NRSV] This is the story of the family of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was shepherding the flock with his brothers; he was a helper to the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives; and Joseph brought a bad report of them to their father.
					\item[VULGATE] Et hæ sunt generationes eius: Ioseph cum sedecim esset annorum, pascebat gregem cum fratribus suis adhuc puer: et erat cum filiis Balæ et Zelphæ uxorum patris sui: accusavitque fratres suos apud patrem crimine pessimo.
					% % \item[OTX*]
					% % \item[OTXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXX*]
					% % \item[OTXXXX*]

	% -----

		% % ---
		\paragraph{Genesis 42:1} % *GENESIS-42-1
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-42-1}

			Now when Jacob saw that there was corn in Egypt, Jacob said unto his sons, Why do ye look one upon another?

	\subsubsection{Genesis 50} % *GENESIS-50
	% -----

		% % ---
		\paragraph{Genesis 50:1} % *GENESIS-50-1
		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-50-1}

		% % ---
			\label{GENESIS-50-26}

			So Joseph died, being an hundred and ten years old: and they embalmed him, and he was put in a coffin in Egypt.

			\begin{versebox}
